entry.title: Traffic Premonitions
entry.summary: Exactly a year ago, an ambulance in Bangalore hit several people. The next day I was driving my scooter on the road besides an ambulance. The sight of the ambulance reminded me of the news story and I thought to myself, “it could happen to me, I should be careful.” We were stopped at a traffic signal, and I was lost in thoughts about the news. The signal turned green, we started moving, the ambulance took a sharp turn, and ran into me. Thankfully, both of us hit the brakes quite hard and the collision was minor. I got a severe whiplash from the sudden stop, and had to suffer through a backache for the next three months. Later I came to know that I had Covid-19 at the time I was driving, and that was probably why I wasn’t careful enough. In a strange way, the backache caused me to take bed …

entry.summary:
I’ve been watching anime for over 30 years now. After such a long time, I’ve become very selective in choosing which shows to watch. These days I only complete a couple of shows per season. I’m tired and bored of repetitive themes and settings, sequels, long-dragging shows, and in particular the deluge of Isekai anime. My patience wears thin and I drop things I don’t like without a thought. Now, I prefer watching only shows with novel ideas or great execution. entry.title: NimConf 2026: Dates Announced, Registrations Open
entry.summary: The Nim Team is happy to announce the next instalment of NimConf! NimConf 2026 will happen June 20, 2026 in the traditional online format where the talks are pre-recorded and revealed as premiers on YouTube while the viewers can ask questions and the presenter can answer them in the live chat. If you have anything to share with the Nim community, submit your talk proposal before May 10, 2026. The moderators will contact you if your talk is accepted and you’ll have time until June 7, 2026 to record and submit your talk. If you are unsure if your topic fits with the NimConf format, please do submit it anyway: the Nim community is generally open to learn about anything Nim-related from pet project showcases to niche libraries and business usecases. What is NimConf? NimConf is an online community event all about the Nim programming language: language development, its ecosystem, projects created with Nim, business cases enabled with Nim, and so on. Basically, anything Nim-related is a legit topic for a talk. For viewers, it’s a great opportunity to learn about the latest Nim development progress, discover new areas to use Nim for, improve your Nim expertise, and exchange experience with other Nim enthusiasts. For presenters, NimConf is an opportunity to reach out to new audiences, promote your work, collect feedback, and build the community. You can see all the talks from previous years on YouTube: NimConf 2020 NimConf 2021 NimConf 2022 NimConf 2024 Important Dates Talk proposals are accepted until May 10, 2026. Talk recordings must be submitted before June 7, 2026. NimConf 2026 will be held on June 20, 2026.

entry.title: The Loss of the Night Sky
entry.summary: As a child I spent a lot of time looking at the stars. I grew up in a small town in east India in the 90s. This was before the boom of cable TV or internet or social media. Often after doing my homework, I’d go out in my front-yard and look at the stars. I was a bit of astronomy geek back then, obsessed with the night sky. We didn’t have telescopes or cameras or any other equipment, but we had plenty of free time. We used to have frequent electricity cuts (or blackouts as people call them these days) in the hot summers. When the ceiling fans stopped working, we had no choice but to go out in the yard and sit under the dark sky. Living in a small town meant low light and air pollution, so the sky was clear and dark.
